paper.title: Factors influencing austenite stability during Inter-critical annealing and effect on mechanical properties of low-density medium Mn steels
paper.research_type: experimental (with thermodynamic equilibrium predictions and Koistinen-Marburger modelling)
paper.paper_scope: Investigates how the addition of 3 % Al with and without 1 % Si to a Fe-8Mn-0.2C medium-Mn steel affects austenite stability during intercritical annealing (700 °C/1 h + water quenching) and the resulting microstructure, retained austenite fraction, TRIP behaviour and strength-ductility (PSE) combination.

alloys.description: Si-free low-density medium-Mn steel; selected as the maximum Al addition to the Fe-8Mn-0.2C system that still avoids the introduction of δ-ferrite in the intercritical temperature range. Fabricated by vacuum arc melting followed by 4× remelting.
alloys.alloys_notes: Composition given as the nominal formula Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C; concentrations used throughout the paper (e.g. in the Ms equation) are in wt.%. Selected as 'the maximum Al without any δ-ferrite'.

alloys.description: Si-containing low-density medium-Mn steel; addition of 1 % Si to the 3Al system introduces δ-ferrite as an equilibrium phase in the intercritical temperature range. Fabricated by vacuum arc melting followed by 4× remelting.
alloys.alloys_notes: Composition given as the nominal formula Fe–8Mn–3Al–1Si-0.2C; concentrations used in the paper are in wt.%. The 1 % Si addition causes δ-ferrite to appear in the ICT range.

unmapped_findings: Thermodynamic (Thermo-Calc TCFE9) equilibrium calculations were performed on the base Fe–8Mn-0.2C system with systematic Al additions of 0Al, 1Al, 2Al, 3Al, 4Al and 3Al–1Si (Fig. 1); these compositions were only used for phase-fraction/lower-critical-temperature predictions and were not fabricated or tested.

Only the two selected compositions Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C (M1) and Fe–8Mn–3Al–1Si-0.2C (M2) were actually melted, processed and characterized; the lower critical temperature considered for all compositions was 600 °C due to limited Mn diffusion.

Intercritical annealing temperature of 700 °C was selected because it corresponds to ~11 % Mn in austenite for both steels, above which austenite would partially/completely transform to martensite during cooling.
Retained austenite fractions measured by XRD: 5.1 % (M1-HR) and 5.7 % (M2-HR), 45 % (M1-IA) and 19 % (M2-IA); after tensile fracture EBSD gave 6.5 % (M1-IA) and 3.2 % (M2-IA).

Tensile properties: M1-HR UTS 1712 ± 10 MPa with 14.8 ± 0.5 % TE; M1-IA UTS 867 ± 10 MPa with 71.8 ± 0.5 % TE (PSE 61 GPa%); M2-HR UTS 1055 ± 15 MPa with 15.4 ± 0.8 % TE; M2-IA UTS 698 ± 20 MPa with 59.4 ± 0.6 % TE (PSE 41 GPa%).
Calculated Ms temperatures are 319 °C (M1-HR) and 296 °C (M2-HR); Koistinen-Marburger prediction gives ~16 % retained austenite at RT for M1 and ~11 % for M2, both lower than the observed fractions.
TRIP kinetics fitting parameter B (f_gamma = A·exp(-B·epsilon)) was 3.6 for M1 and 3.8 for M2, indicating relatively slower TRIP and higher mechanical stability of austenite in M1.
